summary: Keisho Tsukamoto (1929–2010) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He taught at Rissho University and Tohoku University, and served as President of Hosen Gakuen College from circa 1993 to 1999.

Keisuke Fujii (born 1953) is a historian, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate in engineering at the University of Tokyo. He held multiple academic posts at the University of Tokyo between 1982 and 2018.

Keith Dowman (born 1945) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and trained under traditional teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Anagarika Munindra. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

Keiya Noguchi (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University. He served as a lecturer and professor at Shuchiin University and as an institute director at Taisho University.

Kelsang Gyatso (1931–2022) was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Tashi Lhunpo and Sera monasteries and under Trijang Rinpoche. He taught at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre and founded the New Kadampa Tradition in 1991.

Kelsey Alise Seymour works in Sinology and Japanology. She completed her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair and served as a visiting predoctoral fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (2017–2018).
Kemo Jin (1912–2000) was an Indology, Sinology, and linguistics scholar. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University from 1941 to 1945 and became Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University in 1948.

Ken McLeod (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an M.Sc. at the University of British Columbia, studied under Kalu Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa, taught at Kagyu Dongak Chuling, and founded Unfettered Mind in 1990.

Kendall Marchman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from the University of Florida under Mario Poceski. He held assistant professor posts at Young Harris College (2014–2018) and the University of Georgia (2018).

Kendall Wayne Folkert (1942–1985) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Western Michigan University, the University of Göttingen, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and was an associate professor at Central Michigan University.

Kengo Harimoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass. He has held positions at Mahidol University, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Naples "L'Orientale."
Kenichi Kuranishi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held posts as an associate professor at Taisho University and as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg.
Kenji Ishii (born 1954) is a religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1973 to 1983 and held a post at Kokugakuin University around 1990.
Kenji Kinugawa (born 1952) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1971 to 1980 under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Kenji Matsuo (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Yamagata University from circa 1987 to 2019.

Kenji Shimada (1917–2000) was a scholar in Sinology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1938 to 1941 and later held a researcher post there from circa 1961 to 1980.

Kenji Takahashi is an Indology scholar who conducted exchange doctoral studies at Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop and doctoral work under Diwakar Acharya and Yuko Yokochi. He was a fellow at the University of Naples Federico II (2019–2021).

Kenji Watanabe (born 1949) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held an assistant post at the University of Tokyo from circa 1978 to 1980 and studied under Jozef Deleu from circa 1980 to 1982.
Kenjiu Kasawara (1851–1883) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, where he was taught by Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.
Kenjuro Yanagida (1893–1983) was a philosophy scholar who studied at Yokohama National University and under Kitaro Nishida. He held a post at Hirosaki University from circa 1949 to 1951.
